The Mother of God of the Seven Arrows

Icons

Theotokos

The Mother of God of the Seven Arrows

Semistrelnaya · Seven Swords

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 2:34–35

King James Version · Scripture previews

The OCA distinguishes Seven Arrows from the closely related Softener of Evil Hearts by the arrangement of the swords.

[1] Published source,paragraph 3

What is depicted

This nineteenth-century Russian panel depicts Mary without the Child, with seven blades directed toward her heart and additional saints along the borders. It is a historic example of the named type, not the Vologda shrine’s original image.

[2] Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field title; Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.ImageDescription; Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.DateTimeOriginal; Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Artist; Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Credit; Exact file record File:Семистрельная икона.jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.LicenseShortName

History and tradition

The published account associates the type with a concealed icon near Vologda, a sick man’s reported healing, and wider recognition during the 1830 cholera outbreak. These are the source’s traditional accounts.

[1] Published source,paragraph 4; Published source,paragraph 5

The article identifies the Vologda image with Saint Lazarus Church from 1945. That local provenance is distinguished from the nineteenth-century copy pictured in this profile.

[1] Published source,paragraph 6

Published explanation

The OCA describes four swords on one side and three on the other, contrasting a three-three-one arrangement in related images. It records August 13 and the Sunday of All Saints.

[1] Published source,paragraph 3; Published source,paragraph 9

And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign which shall be spoken against;

(Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.

[3] Luke 2:34–35
